subject: gk
question: Which directive principle provides for a uniform civil code for citizens?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 44**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 44 of the Indian Constitution pertains to the Directive Principles of State Policy.
 
• It mandates the State to endeavor to secure a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) for all citizens across the territory of India.
 
• The objective of Article 44 is to provide uniformity in laws relating to marriage, divorce, inheritance, adoption, and maintenance.
 
• The UCC aims to replace personal laws based on the scriptures and customs of each major religious community in India with a common set of rules governing every citizen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy**

 
 
• The Directive Principles are guidelines or principles given to the federal institutes governing the state of India, to be kept in consideration while framing laws and policies.
 
• They are enumerated in Part IV of the Constitution of India from Articles 36 to 51.
 
• Unlike the Fundamental Rights, these principles are non-justiciable, which means they are not enforceable by any court.
 
• They are aimed at ensuring social and economic democracy in the country.
 
 
 
• **Uniform Civil Code (UCC)**
 
 
• The UCC proposes a single law for the country, applicable to all religious communities in their personal matters such as marriage, divorce, inheritance, and adoption.
 
• It seeks to ensure gender equality and national integration.
 
• The implementation of UCC remains a contentious issue with debates over its impact on religious freedom and cultural diversity.
 
 
 
• **Personal Laws in India**
 
 
• Currently, personal laws in India are governed by the religious texts and customs of various communities.
 
• For instance, Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, and Jains are governed by Hindu personal laws, while Muslims and Christians have their own personal laws.
 
• These laws cover aspects such as marriage, divorce, inheritance, and maintenance.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provisions**
 
 
• The Constitution of India provides for both the protection of religious freedom and the pursuit of a UCC.
 
• Article 25 guarantees freedom of religion, while Article 44 advocates for a UCC.
 
• Balancing these provisions remains a complex issue in the legal and social framework of India.
